name: the limit becomes inclusive, so an index exactly at the cliff is reported as over
edits:
if n_chars > limit:
    if n_chars >= limit:
expect: exactly AT the limit is not over

name: the EMPTY-index arm is severed, so a destroyed index reads as comfortably under budget
expect: an EMPTY index exits 2 too — not a comfortable zero

name: the warn threshold becomes a second literal instead of deriving from the limit
expect: the warn threshold tracks the limit it is given

name: the size is counted in BYTES, the WRONG unit — it is the harness's own character limit (r1 CLAUDE H1); this entry was INVERTED, it used to defend bytes
expect: index_chars counts CHARACTERS, not bytes (multi-byte glyphs)

name: CANNOT RUN collapses onto OK, so an unmeasurable index reports success
edits:
OK, OVER_BUDGET, CANNOT_RUN = 0, 1, 2
OK, OVER_BUDGET, CANNOT_RUN = 0, 1, 0
expect: the three exit codes are the DECLARED values and are pairwise distinct

name: the advisory WARN band starts blocking, which is how a gate gets switched off (#56)
edits:
return {"rc": OK, "state": "warn", **common, "headroom": limit - n_chars,
        return {"rc": OVER_BUDGET, "state": "warn", **common, "headroom": limit - n_chars,
expect: a warning is ADVISORY — it must not block

name: the declared limit drifts away from the harness warning it was read from
expect: LIMIT_CHARS matches the 24.4KB the harness reported

name: INDEX is repointed at another corpus file, so the guard measures the wrong subject (r1 CODEX #2a)
expect: INDEX is the always-loaded index, not some other corpus file

name: main() under-reports the size by one byte, so an index one over the limit passes (r1 CODEX #2b)
edits:
rc, msg = budget_verdict(index_chars(index), limit, shown)
    rc, msg = budget_verdict((index_chars(index) or 1) - 1, limit, shown)
expect: main() fails a file ONE BYTE over, measured end to end

name: the reported path becomes a constant, so a mis-pointed guard reads correct (r1 CODEX #2c)
expect: an OK verdict names the file REPO-RELATIVE, with no absolute prefix

name: the unknown-argument predicate accepts everything, so validation is dead (r1 CODEX #7)
edits:
return [a for a in argv if a != "--self-test"]
    return []
expect: a positional operand counts as unknown, not as an accepted operand

name: the two CANNOT RUN arms are merged, so EMPTY and ABSENT become indistinguishable (r1 CLAUDE H3 mutation G)
edits:
if n_chars is None:
    if n_chars is None or n_chars == 0:
expect: an EMPTY index says EMPTY and an ABSENT one does not

name: relative_to is dropped, so the verdict names an ABSOLUTE path (r1 CLAUDE L3)
expect: an OK verdict names the file REPO-RELATIVE, with no absolute prefix

name: the OVER message prints the TOTAL instead of the overage, which a suffix-vacuous case could not see (r1 CLAUDE N1)
expect: EVERY fact reaches the rendered message, in every state

name: an unreadable index reports EMPTY instead of unreadable — same rc, wrong remedy (r1 CLAUDE N1, same class)
expect: an UNREADABLE index says it could not be read, and does NOT claim to be EMPTY

name: newline translation comes back, so a CRLF index UNDER-counts — the dangerous direction (r2 CODEX #4)
expect: index_chars does NOT translate CRLF away (27 chars, not 18)

name: the overage gains a constant, which every SUBSTRING assertion let through (r2 CODEX #1)
edits: {f['overage']:,} characters of its tail never arrive. Nothing chose what those
{f['overage'] + 1000:,} characters of its tail never arrive. Nothing chose what those
expect: EVERY fact reaches the rendered message, in every state

name: self-test dispatch moves back ABOVE validation, so --self-test swallows a bogus flag (r2 CODEX #2)
expect: validation runs BEFORE dispatch: an unknown flag beside --self-test is refused and the suite is NOT entered

name: WARN_FRACTION drifts by a near-miss a threshold fixture cannot see (r2 CODEX #5)
expect: WARN_FRACTION is the declared 0.90, pinned so a near-miss like 0.9004 cannot slip

name: the warn threshold ROUNDS instead of truncating (r2 CODEX #5)
expect: warn_threshold TRUNCATES rather than rounding (int, not round)

name: UnicodeDecodeError leaves the handler, so an invalid-UTF-8 index crashes (r2 CODEX #5)
expect: an index that is not valid UTF-8 is CANNOT RUN, not a traceback

name: OSError leaves the handler, so a present-but-unreadable index crashes instead of CANNOT RUN
expect: a present-but-unreadable index is CANNOT RUN, not a traceback

name: the OK arm names a LITERAL path instead of the label it was given (r2 CLAUDE H1)
expect: EVERY fact reaches the rendered message, in every state

name: the WARN arm's headroom gains a constant — the arm no case had covered (r2 CLAUDE H2)
expect: EVERY fact reaches the rendered message, in every state

name: render ignores the label it is passed and reads module state instead (r2 CLAUDE H1)
expect: EVERY fact reaches the rendered message, in every state

name: the delimited matcher reverts to a bare substring test, which 414-inside-1,414 defeats
edits:
return re.search(r"(?<![\d,])" + re.escape(val) + r"(?![\d,])", msg) is not None
        return val in msg
expect: a number is matched as a WHOLE token: 414 is NOT found inside 1,414

name: the vacuity precondition always passes, so a self-concealing fixture is accepted
edits:
return [f"{a!r} is inside {b!r}" for a in vals for b in vals if a != b and a in b]
        return []
expect: _vacuous_pairs DETECTS a concealing pair (the 80-inside-1,080 that defeated the first loop)

name: a CANNOT RUN fact set carries a limit the message never shows
edits:
return {"rc": CANNOT_RUN, "state": "empty", "label": label}
        return {"rc": CANNOT_RUN, "state": "empty", "label": label, "limit": limit}
expect: the CANNOT RUN facts name the state and keep the label
